data.text:
The same procedural drift note 207 records, a second time, and recorded before a reviewer
finds it rather than after.

The return at record 251 sent the ticket back to tdd. I did not reset the frontmatter, so
from 251 until the advance at 258 the ticket file said `status: review` with all five
criteria ticked while the journal said tdd, across the round that fixed F51 to F54. The
state is correct as this note is written: 258 advanced to review, the file says review and
the five boxes are ticked, which is the order the receipt requires.

Note 207 recorded the first occurrence and named the cause as Codex having written its own
return, so there was no moment at which I was already editing the file. That was true then
and it is not the cause here: I wrote this return myself and simply did not reset it,
because the next instruction was to fix four findings and I went to them.

What would prevent a third occurrence is making the reset part of recording a return rather
than a thing to remember afterwards. `harness return` knows the ticket is leaving review and
knows which file carries the status; nothing else in the procedure needs a person to hold
two facts at once. That is a harness change and not this ticket's, and it belongs with the
four already recorded against the harness in this journal.

Nothing about the reviewed-tree fingerprint is affected, because it is taken at the review
gate and covers the tree from there.
